user_prompt: A horology exhibit featuring pocket watches from three different centuries
title: Art of Timekeeping
description: Three pocket watches — one from each of the 18th, 19th, and 20th centuries — tell the story of humanity's obsession with measuring time through increasingly refined mechanical ingenuity.

scene.scene_prompt: A warm Victorian study lined with dark wood paneling and brass fixtures, ideal for displaying precision mechanical instruments under soft incandescent light.

objects.label: 18th-Century Pocket Watch
objects.placard_description: This verge-fusee pocket watch from the 1780s represents the pinnacle of hand-crafted horology, with a brass movement regulated by a wheel-and-spring escapement that required daily winding.
objects.image_prompt: antique 18th century pocket watch, hero shot, plain white background, centered, photographic quality, single subject, no text, back cover removed to reveal brass gear movement

objects.label: 19th-Century Pocket Watch
objects.placard_description: A Swiss lever-escapement watch circa 1875, mass-produced using interchangeable machine-cut parts — a revolution that made precision timekeeping accessible to the middle class for the first time.
objects.image_prompt: Victorian 19th century pocket watch, hero shot, plain white background, centered, photographic quality, single subject, no text, back cover removed to reveal intricate lever escapement mechanism

objects.label: 20th-Century Pocket Watch
objects.placard_description: A 1930s railroad-grade pocket watch built to strict accuracy standards mandated by American railway safety regulations, featuring a lever escapement accurate to within 30 seconds per week.
objects.image_prompt: 1930s railroad pocket watch, hero shot, plain white background, centered, photographic quality, single subject, no text, back cover removed to reveal precision lever escapement and balance wheel
